description: Web servers, application servers, message queues, CDNs, and DNS — HTTP errors, response times, and SSL certificates.
name: Application Infrastructure
quickFacts: Forward web server access/error logs and install the appropriate TA for structured field extraction.

useCases.title: HTTP Error Rate Monitoring
useCases.value: Rising error rates signal application issues, backend failures, or attacks. Rapid detection reduces user impact and MTTR.

useCases.title: Response Time Trending
useCases.value: Increasing response times degrade user experience before complete failures occur. Trending enables proactive optimization.

useCases.title: Request Rate Trending
useCases.value: Traffic trending supports capacity planning and identifies unexpected traffic patterns (bot attacks, viral events, traffic drops).

useCases.title: Top Error URIs
useCases.value: Identifies the most problematic endpoints for targeted developer attention. Reduces noise by focusing on high-impact errors.

useCases.title: SSL Certificate Monitoring
useCases.value: Expired SSL certificates cause complete service outage and browser security warnings. Proactive monitoring prevents this entirely avoidable failure.

useCases.title: Upstream Backend Health
useCases.value: Backend server failures behind reverse proxies cause partial service degradation. Detection enables rapid failover response.

useCases.title: Bot and Crawler Detection
useCases.value: Bot traffic inflates metrics and consumes resources. Identification enables accurate capacity planning and bot management policies.

useCases.title: Connection Pool Saturation
useCases.value: Saturated worker threads/processes cause request queuing and timeouts. Monitoring enables proactive scaling.

useCases.title: Slow POST Detection
useCases.value: Slow POST requests often indicate application-level performance issues (large form submissions, file uploads, database writes) distinct from slow GETs.

useCases.title: Configuration Reload Tracking
useCases.value: Configuration changes are a common cause of outages. Tracking reloads enables rapid correlation with incidents.

useCases.title: NGINX Upstream Response Errors
useCases.value: Counts upstream HTTP 5xx and connect/timeout errors from NGINX access/error logs. Isolates reverse-proxy vs origin issues faster than aggregate 5xx alone.

useCases.title: Apache mod_security WAF Blocks
useCases.value: Tracks ModSecurity rule IDs and scores for blocked requests. Supports tuning false positives and detecting attack campaigns.

useCases.title: IIS Worker Process Recycling
useCases.value: Frequent `w3wp` recycles cause session loss and latency spikes. Event Log IDs 5074, 5002, 1011 indicate config, memory, or crash-driven recycles.

useCases.title: SSL Certificate Expiry Countdown
useCases.value: Days-to-expiry dashboard for all TLS endpoints monitored by cert checks. Complements UC-8.1.5 with trend and earliest-expiry focus.

useCases.title: HAProxy Backend Health State
useCases.value: CSV stats `status` (UP/DOWN/MAINT) per server line with weight. Distinct from UC-8.1.6 NGINX-only upstream errors for HAProxy-native shops.

useCases.title: Web Server Thread Pool Exhaustion
useCases.value: IIS `QueueFull`, NGINX worker saturation, or Apache `BusyWorkers` at limit causes queueing. Unified thresholding across stacks.

useCases.title: IIS Web Server Monitoring
useCases.value: IIS access logs provide visibility into web application health — error rates, response times, and request volumes. Critical for web-facing services.

useCases.title: IIS Application Pool Crashes & Recycling
useCases.value: Application pool crashes cause HTTP 503 errors and service outages. Frequent recycling indicates memory leaks or configuration issues in web applications.

useCases.title: JVM Heap Utilization
useCases.value: JVM heap exhaustion causes OutOfMemoryError, crashing the application. Monitoring enables tuning before failures occur.

useCases.title: Garbage Collection Impact
useCases.value: Frequent or long GC pauses cause application latency spikes and request timeouts. Monitoring guides JVM tuning.

useCases.title: Thread Pool Exhaustion
useCases.value: Exhausted thread pools cause request rejection and application unresponsiveness. Detection prevents complete service failure.

useCases.title: Application Error Rate
useCases.value: Application exceptions indicate bugs, integration failures, or environmental issues. Tracking error rate by type guides debugging priority.

useCases.title: Deployment Tracking
useCases.value: Correlating deployments with performance changes is the fastest way to identify deployment-caused regressions. Essential for change management.

useCases.title: Connection Pool Monitoring
useCases.value: Exhausted JDBC/database connection pools cause application errors and cascading failures. Monitoring prevents connection starvation.

useCases.title: Session Count Trending
useCases.value: Active session counts indicate concurrent user load. Trending supports capacity planning and license management.

useCases.title: .NET CLR Performance
useCases.value: CLR performance issues (high GC, exceptions, thread starvation) directly impact .NET application performance. Monitoring guides runtime tuning.

useCases.title: Node.js Event Loop Lag
useCases.value: Event loop lag indicates blocking operations that prevent Node.js from handling requests. Detection enables code-level investigation.

useCases.title: Class Loading Issues
useCases.value: ClassNotFoundException and NoClassDefFoundError indicate deployment or dependency issues that may cause intermittent failures.

useCases.title: PHP-FPM Pool Monitoring
useCases.value: Active/idle process counts, listen queue depth, and slow request detection indicate PHP-FPM capacity and backend saturation. Exhausted pools cause 502 errors and request timeouts.

useCases.title: Tomcat JMX Thread Pool Utilization
useCases.value: Connector thread pool busy percentage and rejected connections indicate Tomcat capacity limits. Exhausted pools cause 503 errors and connection timeouts.

useCases.title: WildFly / JBoss Datasource Pool Usage
useCases.value: JMX datasource pool active/idle/wait connections indicate database connectivity health. Exhausted pools cause application errors and slow transactions.

useCases.title: JVM Garbage Collection Pause Time (STW)
useCases.value: Stop-the-world pause duration percentiles from unified GC logs (G1, ZGC) drive SLA breaches before heap % alerts fire.

useCases.title: .NET CLR Memory Pressure
useCases.value: `# Bytes in all Heaps`, `LOH` size, and `% Time in GC` together indicate memory pressure vs high allocation rate. Refines UC-8.2.8.

useCases.title: Node.js Event Loop Lag (High Resolution)
useCases.value: `eventLoopUtilization` and `delay` histogram from `perf_hooks` or Prometheus `nodejs_eventloop_lag_seconds` for sub-millisecond vs millisecond precision.

useCases.title: Python WSGI Worker Pool Exhaustion
useCases.value: Gunicorn/uWSGI `active workers`, `listening queue`, and `timeout` worker kills indicate saturation or slow upstream (DB).

useCases.title: Tomcat Active Session Count
useCases.value: Session explosion may indicate bot traffic, session fixation abuse, or missing session TTL. Per-context session counts from JMX.

useCases.title: WebLogic Stuck Threads
useCases.value: Stuck thread count >0 blocks request processing and triggers health check failures. Server log `BEA-000337` patterns.

useCases.title: JBoss / WildFly Deployment Failures
useCases.value: Failed deployments leave apps stopped or partial. Log markers `WFLYSRV0026`, `Deployment FAILED` require immediate attention.

useCases.title: Spring Boot Actuator Health Down
useCases.value: `/actuator/health` JSON with `status:DOWN` from liveness/readiness probes. Aggregates component failures (diskSpace, db, redis).

useCases.title: .NET Exception Rate Trending
useCases.value: `# of Exceps Thrown / sec` and first-chance exception logs show error storms after deploys. Complements log-based UC-8.2.4 with runtime counters.

useCases.title: Jira Data Center Performance
useCases.value: JMX metrics, request duration, and attachment storage indicate Jira health. Slow requests frustrate users; disk usage growth risks outages. Enables capacity planning and performance tuning.

useCases.title: Consumer Lag Monitoring
useCases.value: Growing consumer lag means messages aren't being processed fast enough, leading to data staleness and eventual message loss if retention is exceeded.

useCases.title: Queue Depth Trending
useCases.value: Growing queue depths indicate consumers can't keep up or are down. Trending prevents message loss and processing delays.

useCases.title: Broker Health Monitoring
useCases.value: Broker failures cause message loss and application disruption. Health monitoring ensures cluster stability.

useCases.title: Under-Replicated Partitions
useCases.value: Under-replicated partitions mean data is at risk of loss if additional brokers fail. Immediate remediation is required.

useCases.title: Dead Letter Queue Monitoring
useCases.value: Messages in DLQ represent processing failures that need investigation. They may indicate bugs, schema changes, or downstream failures.

useCases.title: Message Throughput Trending
useCases.value: Throughput trending identifies capacity limits and validates scaling decisions. Unexpected drops indicate producer or broker issues.

useCases.title: Topic/Queue Creation Audit
useCases.value: Uncontrolled topic/queue creation can lead to resource sprawl. Audit trail supports governance and cleanup.

useCases.title: Consumer Group Rebalancing
useCases.value: Frequent rebalances cause processing pauses and duplicate message delivery. Detection identifies unstable consumers.

useCases.title: Partition Leader Elections
useCases.value: Frequent leader elections indicate broker instability, causing temporary unavailability for affected partitions.

useCases.title: Message Age Monitoring
useCases.value: Old messages in queues indicate processing delays that may violate SLAs. Age tracking provides a business-relevant metric beyond raw queue depth.

useCases.title: RabbitMQ Queue Monitoring
useCases.value: Queue depth, consumer count, message rate, and unacknowledged messages indicate message processing health. Growing depth or unacked messages signal consumer lag or failures.

useCases.title: ZooKeeper Ensemble Health
useCases.value: Leader election state, outstanding requests, and watch count indicate ZooKeeper stability. Frequent leader changes or growing outstanding requests signal ensemble instability affecting Kafka, HBase,…

useCases.title: Kafka Consumer Lag Monitoring (Consumer Group)
useCases.value: Lag in messages and approximate time lag per partition for each `group.id`. Tightens UC-8.3.1 with `kafka-consumer-groups` export fields.

useCases.title: RabbitMQ Queue Depth Alerts
useCases.value: Per-queue `messages_ready` thresholds with business priority tags. Alert routing by `queue` name pattern (`critical.*`).

useCases.title: Azure Service Bus Dead Letter Monitoring
useCases.value: DLQ message count per topic/subscription and dead-letter reasons (`DeliveryCount`, `ExceptionDescription`) for cloud-native messaging.

useCases.title: Kafka Connect Task Failures
useCases.value: Connector `FAILED` state, task failures, and `offset_commit` errors stop data pipelines. Distinct from broker-only monitoring.

useCases.title: Kafka Topic Partition Skew
useCases.value: Byte size and message count skew across partitions causes hot brokers and uneven consumer lag. Uses `kafka-log-dirs` or broker metrics.

useCases.title: RabbitMQ Memory Alarm
useCases.value: `mem_alarm` blocks publishers when `vm_memory_high_watermark` is hit. Early warning from `memory` and `allocated` fields.

useCases.title: ActiveMQ Broker Store Usage
useCases.value: Persistent store percent used (KahaDB) or JDBC store growth causes broker pause and producer blocking. JMX `StoreLimit` usage.

useCases.title: NATS JetStream Consumer Ack Lag
useCases.value: `NumAckPending`, `NumRedelivered`, and consumer lag for JetStream streams indicate slow consumers or poison messages.

useCases.title: MSMQ Queue Depth Monitoring
useCases.value: Message queue buildup indicates application processing failures. Monitoring queue depth prevents message loss and detects downstream system outages.

useCases.title: API Error Rate by Endpoint
useCases.value: Per-endpoint error rates pinpoint failing services, enabling targeted debugging rather than broad investigation.

useCases.title: API Latency Percentiles
useCases.value: P95/P99 latency reveals the experience of the slowest users. Averages hide tail latency problems.

useCases.title: Rate Limiting Events
useCases.value: Rate limiting indicates consumers exceeding their quotas. May signal API abuse, misconfigured clients, or quota adjustments needed.

useCases.title: Authentication Failures
useCases.value: Authentication failures may indicate credential compromise, API key rotation issues, or brute-force attacks.

useCases.title: Service-to-Service Call Failures
useCases.value: Inter-service communication failures in microservices architectures cascade quickly. Detection enables rapid isolation of failing services.

useCases.title: Circuit Breaker Activations
useCases.value: Circuit breaker trips indicate a downstream service is failing. Quick detection enables proactive communication and remediation.

useCases.title: API Consumer Usage Tracking
useCases.value: Usage tracking per API consumer enables billing, quota management, and partner relationship management.

useCases.title: mTLS Certificate Expiration
useCases.value: Expired mTLS certificates break service-to-service communication, causing complete mesh failures. Proactive monitoring is essential.

useCases.title: HAProxy Backend and Frontend Health
useCases.value: Backend server state, connection queue depth, and HTTP response distribution indicate load balancer effectiveness and backend capacity. Detection of DOWN backends or saturated queues enables rapid fa…

useCases.title: Kong Rate Limit Violations
useCases.value: Kong `rate_limiting` plugin log lines and `429` with `RateLimit-*` headers. Identifies abusive consumers vs tight quotas.

useCases.title: AWS API Gateway 4xx/5xx Trends
useCases.value: CloudWatch `4XXError`, `5XXError`, `Latency` per API stage. Single pane for serverless API frontends.

useCases.title: Apigee Policy Violations
useCases.value: Apigee analytics API or syslog with `fault` policy name (SOAPThreat, JSONThreat, Quota, SpikeArrest) for blocked requests.

useCases.title: API Response Time SLA Breaches
useCases.value: p95/p99 latency from gateway access logs vs documented SLA per route (`/api/v1/orders`). Complements UC-8.4.2 with SLA lookup join.

useCases.title: API Key Abuse Detection
useCases.value: Unusual volume of requests per API key or key used from many distinct IPs/countries in short window.

useCases.title: GraphQL Query Depth Violations
useCases.value: Depth/complexity limit errors from Apollo/GraphQL server logs prevent DoS via deep queries.

useCases.title: API Version Deprecation Tracking
useCases.value: Traffic to `/v1/` deprecated routes vs `/v2/` for migration planning. Header `Sunset` or path-based routing logs.

useCases.title: Cache Hit/Miss Ratio
useCases.value: Cache hit ratio directly measures cache effectiveness. Declining ratio means more backend load and higher latency.

useCases.title: Memory Utilization
useCases.value: Cache memory exhaustion triggers evictions, degrading performance. Monitoring enables timely scaling.

useCases.title: Eviction Rate Trending
useCases.value: High eviction rates mean the cache is too small, causing frequent backend roundtrips. Tracking guides capacity decisions.

useCases.title: Connection Count Monitoring
useCases.value: Approaching connection limits causes client rejections. Monitoring enables proactive limit adjustment.

useCases.title: Replication Lag (Redis)
useCases.value: Redis replication lag affects read consistency for apps reading from replicas. Monitoring ensures data freshness.

useCases.title: Slow Command Detection
useCases.value: Slow Redis commands block the single-threaded event loop, impacting all clients. Detection enables command optimization.

useCases.title: Key Expiration Trending
useCases.value: Monitoring TTL patterns ensures cache freshness strategy is working. Unusual patterns may indicate application bugs.

useCases.title: Memcached Hit Ratio and Eviction Rate
useCases.value: Cache hit ratio and eviction rate measure cache effectiveness and capacity pressure. Declining hit ratio or rising evictions indicate undersized cache or changing access patterns.

useCases.title: Squid Proxy Cache Hit Ratio
useCases.value: Cache HIT/MISS/DENY rates on forward/reverse proxy indicate cache effectiveness and upstream load. Declining ratio increases origin latency and bandwidth.

useCases.title: Varnish Cache Hit Rate and Backend Health
useCases.value: Cache efficiency and backend connection failures indicate Varnish health. Backend failures cause cache misses and user-facing errors.

useCases.title: Synthetic Transaction Monitoring
useCases.value: Simulated multi-step user journeys with timing per step validate end-to-end availability and detect degradation before users report issues. Step-level timing enables pinpointing of slow components.

useCases.title: Website Page Load Time Breakdown
useCases.value: DNS, connect, TLS, TTFB, and download timing per page element enable root cause analysis of slow page loads. Breakdown identifies whether slowness is network, backend, or resource-related.

useCases.title: SSH Service Availability Monitoring
useCases.value: SSH is the primary remote administration channel for Linux and Unix servers. An unresponsive SSH daemon locks out operators and often signals broader system distress (OOM, hung kernel, storage full).…

useCases.title: FTP / SFTP Service Availability Monitoring
useCases.value: FTP and SFTP services support automated file transfer workflows between systems, partners, and legacy integrations. Silent service failures cause missed file deliveries that may not surface until bus…

useCases.title: Envoy Proxy Upstream Health
useCases.value: Upstream cluster health, retry rate, and circuit breaker trips indicate Envoy proxy and backend service health. Detection enables rapid isolation of failing upstreams.

useCases.title: HashiCorp Vault Seal Status and Token Count
useCases.value: Vault health, auto-unseal events, and token creation rate indicate secrets management availability. Sealed Vault blocks all secret access; token anomalies may indicate abuse.

useCases.title: HashiCorp Consul Service Health
useCases.value: Service registration, deregistration, and health check failures indicate Consul service discovery health. Critical checks mean services are unavailable for discovery and routing.

useCases.title: HashiCorp Nomad Job and Allocation Status
useCases.value: Failed allocations and job deployment health indicate Nomad scheduler and workload availability. Failed allocations mean tasks are not running; deployment failures block rollouts.

useCases.title: Asterisk / FreePBX Call Quality and Trunk Status
useCases.value: Call volume, ASR (Answer Seizure Ratio), ACD (Average Call Duration), and trunk registration indicate VoIP/PBX health. Trunk failures block inbound/outbound calls; quality metrics affect user experie…

useCases.title: NTP Stratum Drift
useCases.value: Stratum jumps or large offset indicate bad upstream clock or local drift — affects Kerberos, TLS, and distributed logs.

useCases.title: DNS Recursive Query Volume
useCases.value: Sudden spike in recursive queries on internal resolvers may indicate DDoS, malware, or misconfigured application loops.

useCases.title: TFTP Unauthorized Access
useCases.value: TFTP should be rare in enterprise networks. Any RRQ/WRQ outside PXE scope may indicate data exfil or firmware abuse.

useCases.title: SNMP Community String Audit
useCases.value: Detects use of default `public`/`private` or unauthorized SNMP GETs to network devices for SNMPv2c exposure auditing.

useCases.title: User Session Volume Trending
useCases.value: Daily or weekly active session counts show adoption, campaign effects, and capacity needs before saturation. Seasonal patterns become visible for staffing and infrastructure scale plans.

useCases.title: API Endpoint Latency Percentile Trending
useCases.value: p50, p95, and p99 latency over 30 days highlights tail latency regressions that averages hide. Trends support SLO setting and regression detection after releases.

useCases.title: Application Error Budget Burn Rate Trending
useCases.value: Error budget remaining over a sprint or month shows whether reliability goals are sustainable. Accelerating burn triggers freeze or rollback decisions before users experience widespread outages.

useCases.title: Cache Hit Ratio Trending
useCases.value: Cache hit ratio over 30 days reveals memory sizing issues, key churn, and upstream slowdowns that force more origin fetches. Declining trends often precede latency SLO breaches.

useCases.title: Message Queue Backlog Trending
useCases.value: Queue depth over 7 and 30 days shows sustained consumer lag versus transient spikes. Growth trends drive consumer scaling, partition adds, or poison-message handling before disk limits or SLA misses.
